title: Ops security drop-in: exposure review & secrets rotation (2026-07-21)
body:
Attendees: Noah, Lina, Marcus, Priya, Evan, oncall-rotation (Alex)

Meeting goal: quick operational sync to (1) triage two mid-priority exposures from the dependency scan, (2) confirm secrets rotation rollout for the internal metrics pipeline, and (3) capture follow-ups for a lightweight threat-model addendum for the console feature flag changes.

Agenda:
- Quick status from oncall: recent alerts and false-positive patterns (5m)
- Dependency exposure 1: third-party metrics lib (15m)
- Dependency exposure 2: optional telemetry submodule in a shared SDK (15m)
- Secrets rotation plan: metrics pipeline service account keys (10m)
- Threat-model notes for console flag rollout (10m)
- Actions and owners (5m)

Notes / Discussion:
1) Oncall recap
- Alex: two alerts overnight; both were identical malformed auth attempts against a staging endpoint. No signs of data exfiltration. Pattern looks automated and likely scanner noise. We adjusted WAF rules and suppressed this alert class for staging only.
- Observed a recurring spike in 401 errors correlated with a new Canary job (#canary-debug). Marcus to open a small PR to add more verbose error tagging to distinguish telemetry vs auth failures.

2) Dependency exposure A — metrics-lib v2.3.1 (internal label RDW-DEP-2026-07-A)
- Source: SCA flagged an insecure deserialization issue in the metrics lib (upstream advisory). Upstream issued patch in v2.3.2 but our fork is pinned to 2.3.1 in the dedicated-runtime images.
- Impact: libs used in non-customer-facing worker pipelines; potential RCE risk if untrusted data processed — currently low because inputs are sanitized by the ingestion layer, but exploitation path exists.
- Decision: move to v2.3.2 as immediate mitigation in staging and run test harness. If green, schedule rollout to prod next maintenance window (07/28). If tests fail, apply runtime JVM hardening (sandbox classloader) as stopgap.
- Action items:
  - Marcus: open PR to bump fork + run nightly regression tests (due 2026-07-23).
  - Priya: add synthetic fuzzing job for ingestion sanitizers (due 2026-07-26).

3) Dependency exposure B — telemetry-submodule optional import (RDW-DEP-2026-07-B)
- Source: Internal audit found our shared SDK pulls an optional telemetry submodule that triggers remote connections to a vendor endpoint when certain flags are enabled. SCA flagged that the submodule is transitive and not covered by our BOM.
- Impact: Potential unexpected outbound connections from customer-controlled environments in Private deployments; higher risk for regulatory customers.
- Discussion: three mitigation paths considered — (a) remove optional import and replace with a strict interface, (b) vendor patch to make remote calls opt-in at runtime with clear env var, (c) ship new SDK build without telemetry by default.
- Decision: short-term adopt (b) by adding an explicit env var guard and document in the private-deploy README. Long-term remove the optional import and publish a no-telemetry artifact for private customers.
- Action items:
  - Lina: coordinate with SDK owners to add env-var guard and update docs (due 2026-07-24).
  - Evan: create a checklist for Private deploy onboarding to surface transitive optional deps (due 2026-07-30).

4) Secrets rotation: metrics pipeline service account keys
- Context: Scheduled rotation for metrics SA keys next week. We found one historical key still present in an archived deployment manifest (archive-2025-11). No evidence of use.
- Plan: rotate keys, revoke old, and run smoke tests. Use the new key injection flow (KMS-backed) and update CICD to read from secret-store instead of env. We will proactively notify the small number of self-hosted customers impacted by config changes.
- Risk: brief alert noise from failing canaries; mitigations: staggered rollout and preflight validation in canary cluster.
- Action items:
  - Noah: run rotation runbook and coordinate notices to customers (due 2026-07-27).
  - Marcus + SRE: add a canary preflight that validates secret access before traffic cutover (due 2026-07-25).

5) Threat-model addendum: console feature flag rollout
- Trigger: product plans to add a new server-side feature-flag that will allow dynamic eval of light-weight transforms on debug payloads (non-production). Security requested a short addendum to the existing console threat model to cover eval surfaces and data escapes.
- Notes: recommended to ban arbitrary eval and restrict transform language to a whitelist; ensure logging redaction and opt-in telemetry. Also include a requirement for a policy that any transform which could leak PII must be approved by privacy.
- Owner for addendum: Priya agreed to draft a 1-pager and link into the console rollout PR for review.
- Due: draft by 2026-07-26 for review.

Open questions / items for next meeting:
- Do we want a gated policy in CI that fails builds which add transitive optional deps that perform network calls? (Proposal for next week: implement a lightweight scanner rule.)
- Evaluate whether our BOM generation covers optional transitive modules; if not, add to backlog.

Decisions summary (for changelog):
- Patch metrics-lib to v2.3.2 in fork and plan prod rollout 2026-07-28 if tests pass.
- Add env-var guard to telemetry submodule and publish docs for Private deploys; plan long-term removal of optional import.
- Proceed with scheduled secrets rotation using KMS-backed injection and canary preflight.
- Create a small threat-model addendum for the console flag; no arbitrary eval allowed.

Action items (flat list):
- Marcus Li: bump metrics-lib fork + regression tests (JIRA: SEC-4821) — due 2026-07-23
- Priya Nair: fuzzing job for ingestion sanitizers + threat-model addendum draft — due 2026-07-26
- Lina Gomez: env-var guard + docs for SDK telemetry + update private-deploy checklist — due 2026-07-24
- Evan Zhou: private-deploy dependency checklist + follow-up with platform team — due 2026-07-30
- Noah Patel: run key rotation runbook + customer notices — due 2026-07-27
- Marcus & SRE: canary preflight for secret access — due 2026-07-25

Next sync: ad-hoc follow-ups; standing 30m ops-security drop-in scheduled Thu 2026-07-29 10:00 PT. Please update the Confluence note with outcomes and link back to the PRs listed above.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Consider adding a small test harness that simulates private deployments calling optional vendor endpoints — easier to detect transitive surprises early.
- Keep an eye on canary noise after rotation; we should suppress/annotate known expected failures to avoid oncall fatigue.

Attachments / supporting links added to linked_artifacts above."
